thread:
support-swe: customer escalation — tenant 'acme-photos' seeing widespread 504/502s on hosted API between 11:12-11:20 UTC. Ticket CS-7289. Customers hitting timeouts.

sre-oncall: grabbing graphs now. spike ~120 RPS to that tenant, queue depth on inference-proxy soared. autoscaler did not add pods for ~90s, causing gateway timeouts.

eng-runtime: can you pull KEDA ScaledObject events for that namespace? curious if ScaledObject failed or if HPA stabilized too slowly.

infra: running `kubectl -n inference get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=scaledobject-acme` — seeing repeated warnings about annotation mismatch and a few "Cooldown active, skipping scale" events. past 11:12 there was a 2min gap before scale trigger.

support-swe: customer raw error sample: `502 Bad Gateway - upstream timed out after 60s` and `504 gateway timeout`. They saw degraded UX for ~8 minutes and filed SLA complaint.

sre-oncall: digging into pod logs — pod init is stalling on model download: `GET https://models.redwood/internal/models/acme-photos/v2` returned 503 then exponential backoff. readiness probe waits for model load; pod remained NotReady ~85-130s.

eng-runtime: hypothesis: cold model download + KEDA/HPA interaction. If minReplicas=0, first request triggers scale but model fetch on new pod causes long init. With KEDA cooldown/polling, scale request arrives late. Also check scaledobject metric name — earlier deploy changed metric key to `queue_len_v2` and ScaledObject still referencing `queue_len`. possible mismatch.

infra: quick mitigation applied: bumped Deployment minReplicas to 2 for acme-photos, patched ScaledObject pollInterval to 10s (was 30s), and lowered cooldown to 60s for that tenant. rolling update applied.

eng-runtime: recommend longer-term fixes: (1) bake critical models into container image (model bake) to avoid network fetch at pod start; (2) add prewarm jobs for predicted tenant bursts; (3) add queue-length external metric so KEDA triggers immediately on backlog rather than waiting for rate metric; (4) make readiness probe tolerant to partial functionality so proxy can route while background fetch continues for non-critical models.

customer-success: informed customer of temporary mitigation and that we're monitoring. updated CS-7289 with action items and timeline. asked if they want an SLA credit — they requested follow-up post-mitigation.

deploy-bot: deploy started by infra at 2024-06-15T11:45:23Z — rolling update scaledobject-acme / deployment-acme-photos.

sre-oncall: post-mitigation metrics look better — queue depth down and 504s stopped within 4 minutes of changes. continuing 15m watch.

eng-runtime: created ENG-1291 for model-bake pipeline and ENG-1292 to add queue-length external metric and adjust readiness semantics. assigning to runtime team.

support-swe: captured repro steps in CS ticket: run internal load script (link: https://internal/loadtests/acme-surge) ramp to 120RPS targeting tenant header `X-Tenant: acme-photos`. Observed scale lag ~70-110s before mitigation. added logs and curl traces.

infra: saved event snippet to incident log:
```
Warning  FailedGetScale       scaledobject-acme   failed to get external metric: 404 metric not found
Normal   TriggeredScale      scaledobject-acme   scale to 2 started
Warning  CooldownInEffect    scaledobject-acme   cooldown active, skipping scale
```

sre-oncall: next steps — (A) let infra/eng rollout permanent fixes, (B) monitor for 2h and if spike recurs open P1. tagging @eng-runtime @infra. If customer pursues SLA credit escalate to finance via CS. marking incident P2 and adding timeline to CS ticket.

support-swe: thanks all, will keep CS updated. saving thread to incident archive as 1731234567-lagchain-triage for internal reference.
